body.statement:
On the local no-selection experimental submodel \(S=1\) almost surely and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\), impose \(W\perp Z\mid U\) and Conditions (1)--(3) of Theorem 1 of Shingaki--Kuroki (2023). After the label conversion \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), \(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\), the exact value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals this singleton, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\). As a separate boundary-coverage check, for \(|\mathcal W|=|\mathcal Z|=3\), the explicit datum \((b^{\mathrm{bd}},a^{\mathrm{bd}},T^{\mathrm{bd}},r^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}},s^{\mathrm{bd}},p^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})
e\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{rank}(T^{\mathrm{bd}}_e)=2\) for all \(e\), \(\mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}\) when \(T=T^{\mathrm{bd}}\), compulsory zeros \(a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{11,1}(z_3)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{11,2}(z_1)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{00,2}(z_3)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{00,4}(z_1)=0\), and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\). The relative-open support-face chart that preserves these four zero positions, positivity of every other displayed incident coefficient and every proxy endpoint, the strict order of \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\) on their common line, transversality of the two remaining incident lines, and \(m
e r\) is nonempty and rigid. Because \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}
e m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), the displayed selected datum cannot satisfy \(S=1\) almost surely and is outside the 2023 theorem's experimental conditions.
body.justification: This supporting theorem validates the atlas on the exact experimental overlap and on a fully specified selected assignment-boundary datum.
body.gap: Shingaki--Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate the full response-type vector under no selection, randomized treatment, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation; the cited theorem does not address selected forced-zero cycle fibers.
body.consumer: Experimental users can check agreement with the published plug-in estimand, while selected-data users can verify the separate boundary certificate under the present model.
body.proof_tex:
On the stated experimental submodel, \(S=1\) almost surely implies
\(m=r\), and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\) implies
\(P(U=i\mid X=x)=\pi_i\).  The cited experimental identification lemma says
that Conditions (1)--(3) identify the four response-type probabilities and
that its equations (8)--(13) give a consistent plug-in estimator.  We first
show that these observable conditions also make the larger design-A cycle
fiber target-rigid.

Fix a cell \(e=(x,y)\) with incident response types \(i,j\).  For a proxy
category \(w\), define the cell-conditional matrix
\[
 \widetilde Q_{ew}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&P(W=w\mid E=e)\\
 P(Z=z_1\mid E=e)&P(W=w,Z=z_1\mid E=e)
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix \(Q_{xyw}\) in the cited construction differs only by the positive
cell-probability normalizations, so its relevant determinant vanishes exactly
when \(\det(\widetilde Q_{ew})\) vanishes.
Substituting
\(T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top}\) and expanding the two products
gives
\[
 \det(\widetilde Q_{ew})=K_e\{b_i(w)-b_j(w)\}, \tag{25}
\]
where, on writing \(A_{ei}=\sum_z a_{ei}(z)\) and
\(A_{ej}=\sum_z a_{ej}(z)\),
\[
 K_e=a_{ei}(z_1)A_{ej}-A_{ei}a_{ej}(z_1),
\]
which does not depend on \(w\).  Condition (3) makes the determinant contrast
used by the cited equations nonzero, so \(K_e\ne0\) and \(b_i\ne b_j\).
Thus the determinant ratios are observable direction ratios for
\(\mathcal L_e\), and each \(T_e\) has rank two.  The four separation
inequalities in Condition (3) make the two incident directions used for each
response type distinct.  The nonsingular \(2\)-by-\(2\) systems in equations
(8)--(11) therefore identify the unique intersection of its two incident
lines, namely the common endpoint \(b_i\).

The rank-two orientation atlas is exhaustive.  Once every shared endpoint is
the unique incident-line intersection just obtained, every nonempty oriented
endpoint interval is a singleton.  Formula
\[
 a_{ei}(z)
 =v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h)-b_j(h)}{b_i(h)-b_j(h)},
 \qquad c_{ez}=T_e(\cdot,z)/v_e(z), \tag{26}
\]
for any separating coordinate \(h\), then uniquely fixes the coefficient
rows as well.  Hence the whole cycle fiber has one target value, equal to the
value of the generating experimental SCM.

Under the label conversion
\(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), response consistency and
randomization give
\[
 \mathrm{PN}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
 =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
        {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_4},
 \qquad
 \mathrm{PS}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
 =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
        {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_1+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}. \tag{27}
\]
Positive observed cells make both denominators positive.  Equations
(25)--(27), the cycle-to-SCM lift, and the rank-two atlas prove
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,r)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}. \tag{28}
\]
The all-rank-two branch occurs among the charts enumerated by
\(\mathscr A\), so the exact compiler returns the same singleton.  The cited
plug-in consistency and continuity of \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}\) at the positive
denominators in (27) yield
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})
 \xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}). \tag{29}
\]

We now verify the boundary datum without a genericity argument.  Each listed
\(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is strictly positive and has coordinates summing to
one.  In every cell the two displayed coefficient rows are nonnegative, their
coordinatewise sum is \((1/3,1/3,1/3)\), and they are not proportional.  The
two incident endpoint vectors are distinct.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}})=2
 \quad\text{for every }e. \tag{30}
\]
For every \((w,z)\), at least one incident coefficient is positive, while all
endpoint coordinates are positive; hence every entry of
\(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}}\), and then every entry of \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), is
positive.  Moreover
\[
 \sum_e s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}
 =\frac14\left(\frac18+\frac14+\frac38+\frac12\right)
 =\frac5{16},
 \qquad
 \frac{s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}}{5/16}
 =r_e^{\mathrm{bd}} \tag{31}
\]
cell by cell.  Thus the displayed cycle point and selection law satisfy the
normalization required by the cycle-to-SCM lift, which proves
\(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\).

In simplex coordinates, direct substitution gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}
 =\{b:b(w_2)=1/5\},\qquad
 \mathcal L_{01}=\{b:b(w_1)=1/5\},\qquad
 \mathcal L_{10}=\{b:b(w_3)=1/5\}. \tag{32}
\]
The transverse intersections in (32) pin
\(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_3^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(11\),
the normalized columns at \(z_1,z_3\) are respectively
\(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\); hence the segment constraint puts
the type-\(2\) endpoint on the ray beginning at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) and
pointing away from \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(00\), the corresponding
columns are \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\); hence the same endpoint
lies on the ray beginning at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) and pointing away from
\(b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  Since the strict order on the common line is
\(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\), the two rays meet
only at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  All endpoints are fixed, and (26) fixes every
coefficient.  In particular the four displayed zeros are compulsory and
\[
 \tau_C
 =\left(0+\frac16+\frac13,
          \frac13+\frac16+0\right)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac12\right). \tag{33}
\]
The rank-two atlas and the target-preserving lift prove the asserted
singleton full-SCM target set.

On the relative support face preserving the four zeros, the exposed columns
continue to identify the relevant endpoints.  Positivity of every other
coefficient and endpoint, the strict endpoint order, transversality of the
remaining incident lines, and \(m\ne r\) are strict relative inequalities.
The displayed datum satisfies all of them, so this relative-open chart is
nonempty; the same intersection and ray argument proves its rigidity.
Finally \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}\ne m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), whereas \(S=1\) almost
surely would imply \(P(E\mid S=1)=P(E)\), hence \(r=m\).  The boundary datum
therefore lies outside the experimental conditions.
